clue.text: Company with microphones for stand-up entertainers?

parts.note: mics is the everyday short form of microphones

explanation.surface: A firm supplying microphones to stand-up performers at comedy clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the stand-up entertainers are comedians, not people standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedians who perform stand-up routines are commonly called comics; a synonym.

clue.text: Guns officer's hidden in Greek island

indicators.note: the officer is tucked away within the island's name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
LT abbreviates lieutenant, an officer; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An army officer lying low on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt revolvers are famous American handguns, so the brand name in the plural serves for firearms.

clue.text: Philosopher is entertaining a painter

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them within, so the letter a goes inside

parts.note: John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher amusing a painter, perhaps at a Victorian dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' reads as amusing, but it means holding a guest inside, as a host does.
explanation.definitionFit: John Everett Millais was a Victorian painter and a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: Realise old band leader's being presented

parts.note: Billy Cotton led a popular British dance band in the mid-twentieth century; the 's stands for 'is'
a show that is on is being presented

explanation.surface: A veteran bandleader is finally being shown on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Cotton was a British bandleader and radio and TV entertainer from the 1930s to the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is an informal phrasal verb for coming to understand something, a synonym for realise.

clue.text: Lifer condemned after bearing weapon

indicators.note: the rearranged piece comes after the synonym for bearing, so it is placed second

parts.note: air means bearing or manner, as in an air of confidence

indicators.note: condemned suggests the letters of lifer are wrecked and remade

explanation.surface: A life prisoner, condemned, carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An air rifle is a gun firing pellets by compressed air, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Elected Tory toff going round Rugby is out of place

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: the gentleman's letters encircle the rugby abbreviation

parts.note: a toff is a posh gentleman, a gent
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A posh new Tory MP touring Rugby, the school town, looks out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English town famous for its public school; here it is only the abbreviation for Rugby Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of place does not fit its surroundings, which is what incongruent means; a synonym.

clue.text: German government's writer

definitions.meaning: the Reich was the German state, so the possessive is 'of the Reich'

explanation.surface: The writer of the German government.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as Reich's, it is the German state's; as one word, Kathy Reichs writes crime novels.

clue.text: Plant in independent country once losing millions

parts.note: a free nation is independent

indicators.note: losing means the country's name drops a letter

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A plant growing in a formerly independent country that has lost millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are fragrant flowering plants of the iris family.

clue.text: Vixen set loose near middle of field covering large area

indicators.note: set loose means freed from order, so the letters of vixen set run wild
middle of means the central letter of field is taken

explanation.surface: A female fox let loose near the centre of a field that spans a large area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' turns VIXEN SET into EXTENSIV, and 'middle of' adds E from field.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive describes something spread wide or sizable in scope; a synonym.

clue.text: Film with lots of laughter: it has 'adult' certificate

parts.note: LOL is text-speak for 'laughing out loud'
A was an old British film classification for adult audiences

explanation.surface: A hilarious film rated for adults only.
explanation.walkthrough: The old British A certificate meant adult content; the 1962 film actually got an X, as a blog commenter noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is Stanley Kubrick's 1962 film of the Nabokov novel.

clue.text: Mishap I ultimately witnessed, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the speaking style

parts.note: an accent is a way of pronouncing speech

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of witnessed is taken

explanation.surface: Someone reporting a mishap they finally saw, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' sounds like a stock phrase; it is the container. 'ultimately' gives D from witnessed, which joins I to make ID inside ACCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unlucky event, a synonym for mishap.

clue.text: Pop sensation taped by female group: a French song from the 70s

indicators.note: being taped by something means bound within it, so the shuffled letters sit inside

parts.note: several women could be called 'shes', the plural of she

indicators.note: pop means burst, so the letters of sensation are broken up

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A pop star recorded by a girl band, singing a French song from the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like the music genre but means burst, so it signals the anagram; 'taped by' is the container, and 'female group' is a playful plural of she.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry Jacks had a 1974 worldwide hit with this English version of a Jacques Brel song.

clue.text: Undisclosed number supervising introduction of this government office

indicators.note: in a down clue, supervising means placed above, so the song sits over the next letter

parts.note: something undisclosed is kept secret
an aria is a song, a musical number

indicators.note: introduction means the opening letter of this

explanation.surface: A secret figure overseeing the launch of this government department.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is an administrative office of an organisation or government.

clue.text: Upset on one occasion by record? Right

indicators.note: by means next to, so the record sits beside the occasion word

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
once means on one occasion

explanation.surface: Someone upset once by a record, wondering if that is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert is to unsettle or fluster someone, a synonym for upset as a verb.

clue.text: Reckless old man imprisons sappers? Wrong

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold within, so the engineers go inside

parts.note: an old man is slang for a father, dad
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers
evil is wrong, wickedness

explanation.surface: A rash father locks up some army engineers; was that wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers, so the Royal Engineers (RE) stand for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a daredevil stunt, it means boldly reckless.

clue.text: Country, one hit hard in revolution

indicators.note: turning round in revolution means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to lam is to thrash or hit hard

explanation.surface: A country where one is badly hurt during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising, but here it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Old Dutch flying creature, bird-like

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A bird-like flying animal from old Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Batavi were an ancient people of the Netherlands, so Batavian has long meant Dutch.

clue.text: Travellers returning through Glamorgan

indicators.note: returning means the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters sit inside, running through the place name

explanation.surface: Travellers heading back home through Glamorgan in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' finds AMOR in Glamorgan, and 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roma are a traditionally itinerant people, so travellers is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: Exist in brand-new tower

indicators.note: in places the verb inside the word for brand-new

parts.note: in mint condition means as new
to be, so 'are' means exist

explanation.surface: Existence in a gleaming new tower block.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque.

clue.text: Sporting contest opening shortly in holiday area

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes within the holiday spot

parts.note: the seaside is a classic British holiday destination

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A sports event opening soon at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like it means 'soon' but trims VENT to VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-a-side match is a rugby or football game with seven players per team.

clue.text: Inexperienced female in class briefly seen by head of English

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of English

explanation.surface: A green young woman in a class shown up by the head of English.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is a naive young woman, especially as a stock role in theatre.

clue.text: Irish writer appearing to eat French cheese

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it in, so the cheese goes inside

parts.note: a performer who is appearing is on
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: An Irish author on stage, seen eating a French cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Flann O'Brien and Edna O'Brien are both noted Irish novelists.

clue.text: Come again to Barnet: garden's flourishing

indicators.note: flourishing suggests growing wild, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to return to Barnet, a London suburb, because the garden is thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come again' looks like a request to repeat yourself; it is a friendly invitation to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a parting farewell asking someone to keep in touch and visit again.

clue.text: Republican supporter in mass meeting

parts.note: an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A Republican backer at a large political gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a large public gathering, typically political; a synonym.

clue.text: Innocent female finding main road round US state

parts.note: a virgin is a chaste young woman

indicators.note: round here means turned round, so the road's letters go backwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; the 1 is read as letter I

explanation.surface: A naive woman finding a main road around an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its digit 1 serves as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a state on the Atlantic coast of America.

clue.text: Notable film director is taking retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Fritz Lang, director of Metropolis

explanation.surface: A distinguished film director is stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or remarkable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Introduction of Theseus in a tale spun in Virgil's style?

indicators.note: spun means the letters are twisted into a new order, as a yarn is spun
introduction means the opening letter of Theseus

explanation.surface: Theseus brought into a story told in the manner of Virgil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' rearranges T, IN and A TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil wrote in Latin, so his style is Latin-derived, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Exhibition centre in some French city

indicators.note: in places the venue's letters inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham

explanation.surface: An exhibition hall in some French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is a large exhibition venue near Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Annecy is a lakeside city in the French Alps.
